title: Myeloid Mutations: MPN Drivers, SF3B1, KIT D816V and CHIP
summary: Learn how JAK2, CALR and MPL divide the Philadelphia-negative MPNs, how an SF3B1 mutation now defines its own MDS type, why KIT D816V needs a highly sensitive assay, and how CHIP differs from CCUS.

reviewer.note: Teaches Ch. 77 Hits 10 (MPN trio JAK2/CALR/MPL), 12 (SF3B1 and the ring-sideroblast threshold), 13 (KIT D816V in systemic mastocytosis) and 14 (CHIP vs CCUS), and Exam Trap 5 (CHIP does not require cytopenias). Checked against WHO 5th edition (Khoury 2022), Luque Paz 2023, Prins 2020, Steensma 2015 (read via a page-fetch tool), Arock 2015 ECNM KIT recommendations (read via a page-fetch tool), Malcovati 2020 (read via a page-fetch tool) and Lee 2024. Two qualifications are recorded: about 10% of MPN patients are triple-negative, so “together >95%” overstates driver coverage; and the 5%/15% ring-sideroblast rule is the WHO 2016 definition, replaced in WHO 2022 and ICC 2022 by a mutation-defined MDS-SF3B1. The ICC 2022 primary paper (Arber 2022) could not be read: the PMC page returned a browser-verification block, so the ICC VAF ≥10% rule is taken from Lee 2024. Not taught: GIST KIT genotypes, the individual CALR type 1/type 2 percentages.

objectives: State the frequency of JAK2, CALR and MPL mutations in PV, ET and PMF, and the next test after a negative JAK2 V617F.
Explain how WHO 2022 and ICC 2022 define MDS with SF3B1 mutation, and how this differs from the WHO 2016 ring-sideroblast rule.
Choose a sufficiently sensitive method for KIT D816V detection in suspected systemic mastocytosis.
Distinguish CHIP from CCUS using VAF and blood counts.

scenes.title: Four myeloid reports
scenes.altText: Invented scenario: four molecular reports arrive together — (1) sustained thrombocytosis, essential thrombocythaemia suspected: JAK2 V617F not detected; (2) anaemia, marrow blasts 2%, ring sideroblasts 8%, SF3B1 mutation at VAF 30%, normal karyotype; (3) suspected systemic mastocytosis: KIT exon 17 by Sanger sequencing, no mutation seen; (4) a 70-year-old with normal blood counts: DNMT3A mutation at VAF 3%. Question token: “Excluded, classified, or just ageing?”

cues.text: Four myeloid reports arrive. A patient with suspected essential thrombocythemia is negative for JAK2 V617F.
A marrow with two percent blasts and eight percent ring sideroblasts carries an SF3B1 mutation.
A suspected mastocytosis shows no KIT mutation by Sanger sequencing.
And a seventy-year-old with normal counts has a DNMT3A mutation at three percent. Excluded, classified, or just ageing?

scenes.title: The MPN driver trio
scenes.altText: Schematic: one signalling switch labelled JAK-STAT with three driver cards. JAK2 (V617F or exon 12): about 98% of PV, about 55% of ET, about 60% of PMF. CALR (+1 frameshift in exon 9): 0% of PV, about 25–30% of ET, 20–30% of PMF; the two commonest CALR mutations are a 52-bp deletion (type 1) and a 5-bp insertion (type 2), together about 85% of CALR mutations. MPL (exon 10): 0% of PV, about 5–7% of ET, 7–10% of PMF. Triple-negative token: about 10% of MPN patients carry none of the three. Drivers are largely mutually exclusive.

cues.text: Philadelphia-negative myeloproliferative neoplasms share one switch: constant JAK-STAT signalling. Three driver genes can flip it. JAK2, as V617F or an exon 12 mutation, is found in about ninety-eight percent of polycythemia vera, and in about half of essential thrombocythemia and primary myelofibrosis.

CALR mutations are frameshifts in exon 9. They are absent in polycythemia vera but found in roughly a quarter of essential thrombocythemia and myelofibrosis. The two commonest are a fifty-two base pair deletion, type one, and a five base pair insertion, type two, together about eighty-five percent of CALR mutations.
MPL mutations in exon 10 add a few percent more: about five to seven percent of essential thrombocythemia and seven to ten percent of myelofibrosis. The three drivers rarely occur together.
And about one in ten patients is triple-negative: none of the three is found. So a negative JAK2 result means test CALR and MPL next, and a negative panel still does not exclude the disease.

scenes.title: SF3B1 and CHIP: definitions moved
scenes.altText: SF3B1 card, three rows: WHO 2016 — MDS with ring sideroblasts at ≥5% ring sideroblasts if SF3B1 is mutated, otherwise ≥15%; WHO 2022 — MDS with low blasts and SF3B1 mutation (MDS-SF3B1): blasts <5% marrow and <2% blood, no del(5q), monosomy 7 or complex karyotype; ≥15% ring sideroblasts may substitute for the mutation; ICC 2022 — requires SF3B1 VAF ≥10%. CHIP vs CCUS cards (WHO 2022): CHIP = somatic mutation of a myeloid-malignancy gene at VAF ≥2% (≥4% for X-linked genes in males) without a diagnosed haematologic disorder or unexplained cytopenia; CCUS = CHIP plus persistent unexplained cytopenia not meeting criteria for a myeloid neoplasm. Cytopenia: Hb <13 g/dL men, <12 g/dL women; ANC <1.8 × 10⁹/L; platelets <150 × 10⁹/L.

cues.text: Two definitions have moved. Under the 2016 WHO classification, an SF3B1 mutation lowered the ring sideroblast threshold for MDS with ring sideroblasts from fifteen percent to five percent.

The 2022 WHO classification goes further: MDS with low blasts and SF3B1 mutation is defined by the mutation itself, with no ring sideroblast count needed. Fifteen percent ring sideroblasts can stand in when no SF3B1 mutation is found. The International Consensus Classification also requires a variant allele fraction of at least ten percent.

Clonal hematopoiesis of indeterminate potential, CHIP, is a myeloid-malignancy gene mutation at a variant allele fraction of two percent or more, four percent for X-linked genes in males, in someone with no blood disorder and no unexplained cytopenia.
Add a persistent, unexplained cytopenia that does not meet criteria for a myeloid neoplasm, and the same clone becomes CCUS, clonal cytopenia of undetermined significance.

scenes.title: KIT D816V and the hook answers
scenes.altText: KIT card: a codon 816 point mutation in >90% of systemic mastocytosis (WHO 2022); KIT D816V in >80% (ECNM 2015). Mutant allele level is often below 1%. Sanger sequencing sensitivity about 10–20% (false negatives); allele-specific qPCR detects <0.01% mutant cells. Screen peripheral blood; examine bone marrow for a full work-up. D816V confers imatinib resistance. WHO 2022: D816V VAF ≥10% in marrow or blood is a B-finding. Hook answers: (1) test CALR and MPL; ~10% triple-negative; (2) MDS-SF3B1 under WHO 2022 (and MDS-RS under WHO 2016 since RS ≥5% with SF3B1); (3) Sanger negative does not exclude SM — use allele-specific qPCR; (4) CHIP.

cues.text: In systemic mastocytosis, a KIT codon 816 mutation, most often D816V, is found in more than ninety percent of patients. But the mutant allele level is often below one percent of cells.

Sanger sequencing only sees about ten to twenty percent mutant allele, so it misses many cases. Allele-specific quantitative PCR can detect below 0.01 percent. D816V also makes KIT resistant to imatinib.
Back to the hook. The JAK2-negative thrombocytosis needs CALR and MPL testing. The SF3B1-mutated marrow with low blasts is MDS with SF3B1 mutation under WHO 2022.
The Sanger-negative mastocytosis needs a sensitive allele-specific assay. And the seventy-year-old with normal counts and a three percent DNMT3A clone has CHIP, not a diagnosis of MDS.

scenes.title: Three classic traps
scenes.altText: Three trap cards: “CHIP requires cytopenias” (✓ CHIP means no haematologic disorder and no unexplained cytopenia; with persistent unexplained cytopenia it is CCUS); “JAK2-negative excludes an MPN” (✓ test CALR and MPL; about 10% are triple-negative); “Sanger-negative KIT excludes mastocytosis” (✓ mutant allele is often <1%; use allele-specific qPCR).

cues.text: Trap one: CHIP requires cytopenias. No: CHIP means no blood disorder and no unexplained cytopenia. Add a persistent, unexplained cytopenia and it becomes CCUS.
Trap two: a negative JAK2 result excludes a myeloproliferative neoplasm. No: test CALR and MPL, and remember about ten percent are triple-negative.
Trap three: a negative KIT Sanger result excludes mastocytosis. No: the mutant allele is often below one percent, so use a sensitive allele-specific assay.

props.title: ✗ “CHIP requires cytopenias.”
lines: ✓ No unexplained cytopenia; with one = CCUS

scenes.title: One switch, three fingers
scenes.altText: Memory aid: “One JAK-STAT switch, three fingers that press it: JAK2, CALR, MPL. A clone that only whispers (VAF ≥2%, normal counts) is CHIP; a whisper with a cough (cytopenia) is CCUS.” Tokens: switch = JAK-STAT · fingers = JAK2 / CALR / MPL · whisper = CHIP · cough = CCUS. A card lists where the aid breaks.

cues.text: Memory aid: one JAK-STAT switch, three fingers that press it, JAK2, CALR and MPL. A clone that only whispers, at two percent or more with normal counts, is CHIP. A whisper with a cough, a cytopenia, is CCUS.

Where it breaks: about one in ten patients is triple-negative, so no finger is found; JAK2 V617F can itself be a CHIP clone without any neoplasm; and the CHIP threshold is four percent for X-linked genes in males.

scenes.title: Takeaway
scenes.altText: Two tokens: “JAK2 → CALR → MPL · ~10% triple-negative · SF3B1 defines MDS-SF3B1”, “KIT D816V: sensitive assay · CHIP = VAF ≥2% + normal counts; cytopenia → CCUS”.

cues.text: JAK2, CALR and MPL drive most Philadelphia-negative myeloproliferative neoplasms but about one in ten is triple-negative, an SF3B1 mutation now defines its own low-blast MDS type, KIT D816V needs a highly sensitive assay, and a myeloid mutation at 2% or more is CHIP only when there is no blood disorder and no unexplained cytopenia.

props.label: JAK2 → CALR → MPL · ~10% triple-negative · SF3B1 defines MDS
KIT D816V: sensitive assay · CHIP ≥ 2% + normal counts

explanation.what: Plain language: a few mutations name most myeloid neoplasms. Three genes drive most myeloproliferative neoplasms, a splicing-gene mutation marks one type of MDS, one KIT mutation marks mastocytosis, and small mutant clones in healthy older people are a precursor state rather than a disease. Scientific terms: JAK2 V617F, JAK2 exon 12, CALR exon 9 frameshift (type 1 52-bp deletion, type 2 5-bp insertion), MPL exon 10, triple-negative MPN, JAK-STAT signalling, MDS with low blasts and SF3B1 mutation (MDS-SF3B1), ring sideroblasts, KIT D816V, allele-specific quantitative PCR (ASO-qPCR), variant allele fraction (VAF), clonal haematopoiesis of indeterminate potential (CHIP), clonal cytopenia of undetermined significance (CCUS).
explanation.why: JAK2, CALR and MPL mutations all switch on JAK-STAT signalling and are WHO/ICC diagnostic criteria, so testing them in order raises diagnostic yield. SF3B1-mutant MDS is a distinct disease type, which is why the classifications now define it by genotype. Mast cell burden is often low, so insensitive assays give false negatives. Somatic mutations are common with ageing, so a mutation alone is not enough to diagnose a neoplasm.
explanation.measure: MPN: JAK2 (V617F or exon 12) ~98% PV, ~55% ET, ~60% PMF; CALR 0% PV, ~25–30% ET, 20–30% PMF; MPL ~5–7% ET, 7–10% PMF; ~10% triple-negative. MDS-SF3B1 (WHO 2022): blasts <5% marrow and <2% blood; no del(5q), monosomy 7 or complex karyotype; ≥15% ring sideroblasts may substitute for the mutation; ICC requires SF3B1 VAF ≥10%. KIT: codon 816 mutation in >90% of SM; allele level often <1%; Sanger ~10–20% sensitivity; ASO-qPCR <0.01%. CHIP: myeloid-gene VAF ≥2% (≥4% X-linked in males), no haematologic disorder or unexplained cytopenia; progression about 0.5–1% per year. CCUS: CHIP plus persistent unexplained cytopenia (Hb <13 g/dL men, <12 g/dL women; ANC <1.8 × 10⁹/L; platelets <150 × 10⁹/L).
explanation.differs: CHIP (normal counts) vs CCUS (unexplained cytopenia, criteria for a neoplasm not met) vs MDS (cytopenia plus dysplasia or a defining genetic lesion); WHO 2016 MDS-RS (ring-sideroblast count, lowered to 5% with SF3B1) vs WHO 2022 MDS-SF3B1 (mutation-defined); Sanger sequencing vs allele-specific qPCR for low-level KIT D816V.
explanation.examAngle: Expect: next test after a negative JAK2 V617F in ET or PMF, classify a normal-count patient with a small myeloid clone, pick the method for KIT D816V, or name the MDS type for an SF3B1-mutated low-blast marrow.

questions.stem: A patient with sustained thrombocytosis and suspected essential thrombocythemia is negative for JAK2 V617F. Which test adds the most diagnostic yield next?

options.text: CALR exon 9 mutation testing, then MPL exon 10
options.rationale: Correct. CALR mutations occur in about a quarter of ET and MPL in a few percent more; both are WHO/ICC diagnostic criteria.

options.text: No further testing; an MPN is excluded
options.rationale: Incorrect. About half of ET lacks JAK2 V617F, and about 10% of MPN patients are triple-negative.

options.text: JAK2 exon 12 testing as the next step
options.rationale: Incorrect. WHO 2022 lists JAK2 exon 12 mutations among the polycythemia vera criteria; in suspected ET the other driver genes to test are CALR and MPL.
Incorrect. KIT D816V marks systemic mastocytosis, not essential thrombocythemia.

questions.stem: A 70-year-old has a normal complete blood count. Sequencing of blood shows a TET2 mutation at a variant allele fraction of 4%, and there is no known haematologic disorder. How is this best classified?

options.rationale: Correct. A myeloid-malignancy gene mutation at VAF ≥2% without a haematologic disorder or unexplained cytopenia is CHIP.
Incorrect. CCUS requires a persistent, unexplained cytopenia; the counts here are normal.
Incorrect. MDS is defined by cytopenia with dysplasia or a defining genetic lesion; a somatic mutation alone is not sufficient.

options.text: Not reportable, because a 4% VAF is below the CHIP threshold
options.rationale: Incorrect. The CHIP threshold is ≥2% (≥4% only for X-linked genes in males), so 4% meets it.

questions.stem: An anaemic patient’s marrow has 2% blasts, 8% ring sideroblasts and a normal karyotype; sequencing shows an SF3B1 mutation at VAF 30%. Under the WHO 2022 classification, what is the diagnosis?

options.text: MDS with low blasts and SF3B1 mutation
options.rationale: Correct. In WHO 2022 the SF3B1 mutation defines this type in a low-blast MDS without del(5q), monosomy 7 or complex karyotype; no ring-sideroblast count is needed.

options.text: Not SF3B1-type MDS, because ring sideroblasts are below 15%
options.rationale: Incorrect. The 15% count only substitutes for the mutation when no SF3B1 mutation is found.
Incorrect. MDS-IB1 needs 5–9% marrow or 2–4% blood blasts; marrow blasts here are 2%.

options.text: CHIP, because a mutation is present without other findings
options.rationale: Incorrect. The patient is anaemic and has a defining SF3B1 mutation in a low-blast marrow, which is MDS rather than a precursor state.

accuracyFlags.issue: Ch. 77 Hit 10 says JAK2, CALR and MPL together account for >95% of Philadelphia-negative MPN. Luque Paz 2023 reports that about 10% of MPN patients are triple-negative, and gives MPL as about 5–7% of ET (reviewer: 3–5%). The lesson teaches ~10% triple-negative (register flag rv-mpn-triple-negative).

Ch. 77 Hit 12 gives the WHO 2016 rule (SF3B1 lowers the MDS-RS threshold from 15% to 5%). WHO 2022 defines MDS with low blasts and SF3B1 mutation by the mutation, with ≥15% ring sideroblasts only as a substitute, and ICC 2022 requires SF3B1 VAF ≥10% with no ring-sideroblast requirement (register flag rv-sf3b1-rs-threshold).

The ICC 2022 primary paper (PMC9479031) was blocked by a browser-verification page and was not read. No human expert has reviewed this lesson.
